summary: Verified the one-time retroactive backfill script backend/scripts/backfill_low_confidence_council_logs_2026_08_25.py end-to-end. All 6 pytest checks pass. Independently confirmed: (1) script is idempotent — re-running dry-run finds candidates_scanned=1000, total_flagged=0, fallback_message_matches=0, mismatch_detector_matches=0; (2) dry-run does NOT mutate the DB (count_documents({low_confidence:True}) is unchanged before/after); (3) the 6 rows main agent flagged have BOTH low_confidence=True AND low_confidence_backfilled=True, and each of them re-passes one of the two detection signals (3 matched FALLBACK_MESSAGE exact-equality, 3 matched response_seems_mismatched — matches main agent's tally exactly); (4) services.ora_council_retriever._quality_filter returns False for all 6; (5) get_retriever_stats() after _rebuild_index() shows corpus_rows=1000, unique_users=8, unique_projects=5, modes_indexed=['A','D','E'] — matches main agent's observation; (6) none of the 6 backfilled _ids appear in the in-memory _index after rebuild. Backend /api/health = 200, no errors in supervisor logs.

minor.issue: Doc/expectation mismatch in review request: request expected 'already_flagged_skipped'==6 on re-run, but the Mongo query itself filters low_confidence:{$ne: True}, so already-flagged rows never enter the cursor and already_flagged_skipped stays 0. The doc.get('low_confidence') is True defensive branch inside the loop is effectively dead code. Idempotency is correctly achieved via the query filter (total_flagged=0 on re-run), but the counter naming is misleading. Cosmetic only.

action_items: Optional cosmetic: either remove the dead 'already_flagged_skipped' counter/branch in the script, or widen the query to include low_confidence:True rows so the counter actually reflects skipped-because-already-flagged. Not blocking — idempotency is already correct via the query.
critical_code_review_comments: Idempotency is guaranteed by the query filter {low_confidence:{$ne:True}}, which is the right approach (avoids scanning already-processed docs). The in-loop `if doc.get('low_confidence') is True` check is unreachable given that query and could be removed.
Script correctly uses os.environ[...] with no defaults (fails fast on missing config) and only writes when --apply is passed. Matches the fix_ttl_field_types_2026_08_27.py convention.
Two-flag design (low_confidence + low_confidence_backfilled) is clean — makes retroactive vs live-flagged rows distinguishable for future audits.
Script is not registered in main.py startup — correct, this is meant to be a one-shot manual migration.
